SMTO-CFG-0094 — SMTO couldn't save your Skill permission answer

GUID: 13b33a26-02b7-5334-ab00-9f20ebea6be0
Slug: capability-activation-commit-failed
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save your answer to a Skill permission question but couldn't confirm that it was saved. Until it is, the Skill settings you had before still apply.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and look at the task. If the question is gone and the task has moved on, your answer was saved and you're done. The save may have finished even though SMTO couldn't confirm it, so answering twice isn't needed.
  2. If the same question is still showing, answer it again with Allow for this conversation (or Allow for this task) or Don't allow. A question that is still open means the earlier answer wasn't saved, so answering again is safe.
  3. If saving fails again, ask the person who manages SMTO to check that the computer running SMTO has free disk space and that SMTO can write to its data folder. SMTO can't save answers when it can't write to its data folder.

What success looks like

  • The question disappears and the task continues with the Skill on or off, as you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or delete SMTO's data folder to clear the question; it holds your conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The capability grant decision could not be confirmed as committed; the previous conversation capability policy and run authority remain in effect (no current code path raises this kind directly; unexpected failures propagate from the grant transaction).

What this means

  • This retained commit-failure kind has no direct current producer; current grant handling relies on its owning transaction/savepoint and propagates unexpected failures. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained commit-failure kind has no direct current producer; current grant handling relies on its owning transaction/savepoint and propagates unexpected failures.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the durable grant, policy revision and existing transaction result rather than assuming which persistence stage failed.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's capability_grants entry, the conversation capability revision and any capability_grant_child continuation to determine whether the decision committed. Fix the underlying storage or transaction error shown in the Server log, then re-answer only if the grant is still in the prompted state.
  • Reconcile the existing grant result and repair the established failure before another approval attempt.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • Current saved authority confirms whether the original decision committed.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
